cards.title: Scheduling 200 agents
items: Earliest deadline first: 200 briefs due 07:30 spread over 90 min
Provider: requests and tokens per minute; wait or switch model
Tenant: concurrency limit per tenant
Host: 8 containers, 0.5 CPU and 512 MB each
429: backoff with jitter, then local model; quota split across tenants
Predicted missed deadline escalates to a person

cards.title: Sandbox
items: Regular user, read-only filesystem, 64 MB scratch disk
No extra capabilities or privilege escalation, default seccomp
Process, CPU and memory limits; py.exec as a subprocess
Run token is tied to the container IP and is not a credential
Cross-tenant read, CONNECT tunnel, direct model call: policy_denied

cards.title: Failure and resume
items: Step key: run_id, step_no, hash of messages and tool args
STARTED before the call, COMPLETED or FAILED before the reply
SUCCEEDED only with an artifact citing own-tenant message IDs
Auto-resume: new container, same run_id, skips completed steps
Rerun a step that died STARTED and log cost_uncertain
Hand to a person: STOPPED_LOOP, STOPPED_BUDGET, 3 resumes, all models down, third denial

cards.title: Tenants, evals, memory
items: One membership per user: viewer, approver or admin
Proxy tenant scope plus Postgres RLS; unscoped query returns no rows
Evals: 20+ recorded cases, hard checks, temperature-0 judge, drop of 0.3 or less
Memory: cursor, facts, run summaries as quoted data; cursor moves on SUCCEEDED
Panel (design only): three models, two rounds, minority view kept

cards.title: Drafts and approval
items: Agents write drafts and cannot send
send needs an approver in the same tenant
Message-ID from the draft ID, so a replay never sends twice
External or attached drafts are flagged and need their own approval

cards.title: Not building, and hardening
items: Not built: live connectors, web UI, OIDC, replica, multi-host, panel
Shared kernel: no gVisor or microVMs; a kernel exploit could reach other tenants
Weakest part: the proxy holds every credential, tenant map and budget
1 Detect leaks: canary IDs and a fuzzer
2 Firecracker microVM per run from a warm pool
3 Vault and broker: five-minute, one-tenant tokens
4 Gateway, broker, ledger over mutual TLS, failing closed
5 Synchronous Postgres replica and lease fences
